name: thurston_eight_geometries

phase_0.boundary_condition: Thurston's classification theorem establishing exactly eight 3D geometries

VINIT.justification: Initial topological space before geometric structure assignment

TANCH.justification: Final boundary condition completing the classification system

AFWD.justification: Forward operation endowing manifold with local isometry group

AREV.justification: Reverse operation breaking manifolds into prime summands

FSPLIT.justification: Splitting H²×ℝ or S²×ℝ geometries into base components

FFUSE.justification: Reconstituting product geometries from factor geometries

EVALT.justification: Affirmative evaluation of geometric structure compatibility

ENGAGR.justification: Paradice state where manifold admits both geometric interpretations

IFIX.justification: Permanent record of final geometric classification

phase_3.true_description: Manifold successfully equipped with one of eight Thurston geometries
phase_3.false_description: Manifold failing geometric structure compatibility tests
phase_3.both_description: Manifold exhibiting properties of multiple geometries prior to final classification

steps.domain_action: Decompose into prime manifolds via connected sum
Apply geometric structure candidate to first prime component
Factor product geometries into base components
Reconstruct product geometries from validated factors
Perform canonical decomposition of non-product components
Reject geometries with incompatible fundamental groups
Compose remaining geometric structures via connected sum
Handle Nil/Solv geometry ambiguity through topological invariants
Confirm geometric uniqueness through isometry group analysis
Seal system with classification completeness proof

phase_5.memory_mechanism: Topological invariants stored as Betti numbers and group cohomology
phase_5.alfs_store: Thurston's original 1982 paper 'Three-Dimensional Manifolds, Kleinian Groups and Hyperbolic Geometry'

phase_6.cycle_cost: Computational complexity of geometric structure verification
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: High-entropy state of unclassified topological possibilities
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Low-entropy state of eight discrete geometric classifications
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — Classification preserves topological information through structure assignment rather than destruction
